evidence.excerpt: Irradiance and temperature sensors deployed in field PV monitoring stations drift gradually due to soiling, ageing, and mechanical misalignment, introducing systematic bias into SCADA telemetry that is difficult to distinguish from true plant degradation. This paper trains a convolutional autoencoder on the first twelve months of records from twelve monitoring stations, treating this period as nominally calibrated, and then monitors reconstruction error on subsequent 36 months of data. Three types of drift—irradiance pyranometer zero-offset, temperature sensor gain shift, and voltage divider ageing—were induced artificially in a hardware-in-the-loop testbed to generate labelled validation data. The autoencoder flagged all three drift types within a two-week detection lag at an average false positive rate of 8 %. A lightweight rule-based filter using interquartile consistency across co-located sensors reduced false positives to 3 % without increasing the detection lag. The method was subsequently applied to two production archives where unconfirmed drift events were identified.
